content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Presets stripe

Each of the mentioned platforms — Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle — offers a set of features that can seem appealing at first. However, they are built on a model of control and dependence. Stripe, for example, operates in 46 countries, but this also means that creators in the remaining 149 countries are locked out. PayPal's suspension policy can freeze your funds for up to 180 days. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle may seem like alternatives, but they have their own set of restrictions and limitations. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure stack like the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) — Stack 02 deployed in 48 hours, Cloudflare Pages + Workers + Supabase + NOWPayments, 5 products loaded, SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured, end-to-end tested before handoff, 30-day support — offers creators a permanent structural alternative. This stack is not a workaround, but a base-layer infrastructure solution that gives creators control and ownership.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

The problem of restricted countries is a significant one. Stripe's limitations mean that creators in many countries are locked out of the platform. PayPal's suspension policy can freeze funds for up to 180 days, affecting creators worldwide. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle may seem like alternatives, but they also have their own set of restrictions. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure stack like the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is designed to operate in any country, regardless of the platform's restrictions. This means that creators can sell their digital products without worrying about being locked out of a platform.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, the options are limited. Stripe and PayPal charge high fees, while Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy have their own sets of fees. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure stack like the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) offers a low fee of 0.5% with NOWPayments, which is a significant advantage for creators. Additionally, the stack is designed to automate payment processing, reducing the real costs associated with manual processing.
Stripe's geographic exclusion list is a deliberate infrastructure decision — not a temporary gap waiting to be fixed.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Ownership, automation, and delivery are critical aspects of a commerce infrastructure stack. With Stripe and PayPal, creators are reliant on the platform to handle payment processing, which means that they have no control over their own data. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure stack like the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) gives creators full ownership of their data, automating payment processing and delivery. This means that creators can focus on their products and customers, without worrying about the underlying infrastructure.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

Ultimately, the choice of architecture depends on your specific situation. If you're a creator in a restricted country, a sovereign commerce infrastructure stack like the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is the only option. If you're looking for a low-fee solution with automation, the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is the best choice. By choosing the right architecture, creators can ensure that their digital products are sold securely, efficiently, and with full control over their data.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
Sovereign infrastructure means no single platform decision can cut off your income — the store runs under your own accounts.

Creators researching Stripe and PayPal alternatives consistently arrive at the same conclusion: the problem is not finding a single substitute payment processor — it is rebuilding the entire commerce stack on infrastructure that does not inherit the restrictions of the conventional financial system. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 is the complete deployment: Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus Supabase plus NOWPayments, deployed in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff, 30-day support included. If you want to build it yourself, the Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents both Stack 01 and Stack 02 in complete detail with full source code. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Accept that no workaround inside conventional payment infrastructure is durable — platforms actively close gaps as they discover them. Create a NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as your starting point — these cover the widest range of buyers in restricted markets. Choose your stack: Stack 01 for a self-deployed free setup using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, Stack 02 for the Edge Stack deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours. Configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint URL in your IPN settings pointing to your backend. Upload your product files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the full pipeline: webhook received, transaction verified on-chain, order logged, delivery email sent, download link working. Share your store URL only after the mainnet test passes cleanly.
